explanation: Taking your shoes off when entering a Russian home is standard practice, largely to keep floors clean of mud, snow, and street grime, especially during winter. Hosts commonly offer guests slippers (tapochki) to wear instead, and it's polite to accept them.
local_tip: Remove your shoes just inside the door unless your host specifically tells you to keep them on, and accept any slippers offered.

also_check.note: Shoe removal is mandatory and ritualized, with separate slippers often used just for the bathroom.
Shoe removal varies by household; many hosts don't expect it unless asked.
Shoe-removal customs vary by household and aren't as consistently expected as in Russia or Japan.

sources.title: What to Expect When Visiting a Russian Home: Hospitality Dos and Don'ts
